name: Namq Café
why: Open around the clock and famous for its 'Namq cake' — a 24-hour spot with a big food-plus-coffee menu is exactly where a paper menu wears out fastest; a bilingual QR menu keeps late-night study crowd

name: Wooden Coffee
why: A minimalist, design-led café — a clean QR e-menu matches its aesthetic far better than laminated cards, and lets it update seasonal brews without reprinting.

name: Najd Roastery
why: Riyadh-born roastery selling take-home beans plus espresso, drip and cold coffee — an e-menu can list rotating bean origins and retail bags in Arabic and English, which changes too often for print.

name: Kicksters Coffee
why: A modern independent with bold signature brews — a shareable QR menu doubles as marketing for a small shop competing next to big names like Camel Step in the same district.

name: Jorn Coffee Roasters
why: A respected homegrown precision roaster — single-origin offerings rotate constantly, so a digital menu that updates in minutes beats reprinting cards every time a bean sells out.

name: Las Cafe
why: Two locations (Al Malqa and Al Olaya) — one QR e-menu keeps both branches identical and lets the owner change prices once for both shops.

name: IDMI Coffee
why: A roastery-led café in a quiet residential stretch of Al Yasmin — a process-focused menu (brew methods, origins, tasting notes) is much easier to present bilingually on a phone than on a printed card.

name: BOSS.CO Roastery
why: Curated single-origin brews in a soft-industrial space — its bean lineup changes with each roast, and an e-menu lets it showcase current origins without wasting print runs.

name: Drip Coffee
why: A sleek specialty café in Riyadh's busiest business district — Olaya's mix of Saudi and international office workers makes a bilingual AR/EN QR menu an immediate daily convenience.

name: Yamm Coffee
why: Known for signature drink creations and unique pastries in an Instagrammable space — a QR menu with photos extends that visual identity and is easy to share on social media.

name: Carve Coffee Bar
why: A calm, cozy espresso retreat — small independents like this rarely have any web presence, so a MENU SADAH page is both their menu and their first website.

name: Just a Space
why: A design-focused café where the interior is the brand — a beautifully typeset bilingual e-menu fits the concept, while a laminated sheet undermines it.

name: Crops Coffee
why: Single-origin beans and precision brewing with cupping-led discovery — tasting notes and rotating origins are exactly the kind of content that needs a menu you can edit weekly, not reprint.

name: SoMatcha
why: Founder-led matcha brand with three branches open 6am to 3am — multi-branch consistency plus a young, phone-first customer base makes a shared QR e-menu a natural fit.

name: Key Cafe
why: 24-hour café serving coffee, matcha, juices and top V60 across three branches — round-the-clock service with rotating staff is where a self-serve bilingual menu saves the most explaining.

name: Happyland Matcha
why: New 2025 opening with drinks whisked to order and house-made syrups like miso honey and carrot-cake matcha — a specialty menu this unusual needs descriptions in both Arabic and English so customers kn

name: Kuro
why: A new Japanese-style café serving fluffy pancakes and matcha drinks — an unfamiliar Japanese menu benefits enormously from a photo-rich bilingual QR page that explains each dish.

name: 9th Street Coffee Roasters
why: An independent roaster praised for specialty coffee, healthy food and single-origin organic beans — a combined food-plus-beans menu is complex enough that a searchable digital menu clearly beats print

name: Roof Coffee
why: Brand-new single-floor specialty coffee spot announced via X coffee reviewers; presence is social-only with indoor/outdoor seating photos, no structured menu online.

name: AGRIO Coffee
why: In trial (soft) opening, one floor, indoor seating only; menu (specialty coffee + cheesecakes) exists only in reviewer photos on X — ideal early-stage QR menu client.

name: Razeen Coffee
why: Just-opened neighborhood specialty coffee inside a residential district; only footprint is X/TikTok posts, classic photos-as-menu case.
social: X coverage by @DHDH9933; TikTok discover 'رزين قهوة مختصة الرياض'

name: Qawam
why: Small south-Riyadh specialty cafe with indoor/outdoor sittings promoted only through local X promo accounts; south Riyadh is underserved by menu tech.

name: Harmony Cafe
why: Recent Takhassusi opening pushed heavily by paid TikTok/Instagram reels; desserts and drinks shown only in influencer video, no digital menu.

name: Eya Coffee
why: Two-year-old independent cafe near a metro station whose whole identity lives on its Instagram grid; menu discoverable only via photos and TikTok reviews.

name: Cafe !N
why: Small Olaya coffee spot known for its seating vibe, discovered through Instagram reels; no structured bilingual menu online.

name: VARK
why: Two-branch local concept (signature toasted-bread sandwiches, 5 fillings, plus specialty coffee and desserts) whose menu exists only inside TikTok ad videos — perfect fit for a structured item-list me

name: Chi.Chi
why: Cozy new cafe riding the viral chimney-cake trend, open 4pm-2am; discovery is purely Instagram (@chi.chi.ksa) and word of mouth.

name: Jadeel
why: Independent specialty coffee that just opened a Suwaidi location in west/south Riyadh, an area with few QR-menu adopters; covered in Time Out's Arabic new-cafes roundup.

name: Ralph Cafe
why: New independent cafe featured in Time Out's Arabic new-cafes list for creative coffee in a distinctive setting; social-first presence, no structured online menu found.

name: House of Matcha
why: Small matcha-focused bar riding Riyadh's matcha wave; brand lives on Instagram (@housematcha.sa) and delivery apps, no owned bilingual menu page.

name: ON OFF Coffee
why: Cozy independent spot praised for its matcha latte and coffee in local roundups; social-first small cafe with no structured digital menu found.
social: Featured in Lovin Riyadh matcha roundup
